etymology: 「せい」 is traditionally written with two kanji meaning roughly "what is done". One theory traces it to the Sino-Japanese word しょい ("that which someone has done"), whose reading changed to せい; it originally meant "what (someone) did, the result they caused", and extended to "reason, cause, blame". Because opinions on its origin differ, it is mostly written in kana today.
formation: 「せいで」 = the noun 「せい（所為）」 (the result of what someone did → responsibility) + 「で」 marking cause. “Because A caused it” → attributing the result to A; since 「せい」 itself implies responsibility, the result is usually bad and a tone of blame comes naturally. Adding the question particle 「か」 gives 「せいか」, “perhaps because of A”, making the cause uncertain; 「Aのせいにする」 is “setting” the responsibility on A → blaming A.

similar.title: 〜おかげで
similar.explanation: Also gives a cause, but with the opposite evaluation: 「せいで」 is for bad results with blame, 「おかげで」 for good results with gratitude. 「雨のせいで中止になった」 vs 「雨のおかげで涼しくなった」.

similar.title: 〜せいか
similar.explanation: Same origin: 「せいか」 means “maybe because of ...”, an uncertain cause with a softer tone, usable for both good and bad results: 「年のせいか、疲れやすい」.

similar.title: 〜ために
similar.explanation: Close in the cause use. 「ため」 is a neutral, objective cause, suited to reports and announcements: 「事故のため、電車が遅れた」; 「せいで」 implies blame and should be avoided in formal settings.

meaning: Evaluates something from a person's or organization's standpoint: “for ...”, “to ...”.
connection: Noun + にとって／にとっては／にとっても／にとっての + noun

senses.label: For / to
senses.meaning: A judgment from a person's or organization's point of view: “for ...”, “to ...”. The second part is usually an evaluation like 「大切だ・難しい・ありがたい・問題だ」, not a specific action.
senses.connection: Noun (person / organization) + にとって
examples: To me, this photo is a treasure.
Finding an apartment is tough for international students.

senses.label: For ..., though / also
senses.meaning: 「にとっては」 adds contrast: “for ..., on the other hand”. 「にとっても」 means “for ... as well”.
senses.connection: Noun + にとっては／にとっても
examples: It may be easy for adults, but it's hard for children.
This decision is a big issue for the company as well.

senses.label: For ... (before a noun)
senses.meaning: Before a noun, use 「にとっての」: “... for ...”.
senses.connection: Noun + にとっての + noun
examples: What does happiness mean for a child?
My most precious treasure is my family.

notes: It's followed by an evaluation or judgment (「大切だ」, 「難しい」, 「必要だ」), not by an attitude or action toward someone: ✕ 「先生にとって親切だ」 → ○ 「先生に対して親切だ」.
「にとって」 doesn't express a role: ✕ 「教師にとって、学生を指導する」 → ○ 「教師として、学生を指導する」.
Telling your boss 「部長にとっては簡単でしょう」 amounts to evaluating your superior's ability, which is considered rude in Japan. To hear their view, ask directly: 「部長はどうお考えですか」.

etymology: Made of the case particle 「に」, marking the target, and 「取って」, the te-form of the verb 「取る」 (to take); the old form 「に取りて」 became 「にとって」 through a geminate sound change. Literally "taking it with regard to ...", i.e. "viewed from the standpoint of ...". It is now fully grammaticalized and almost always written in kana.
formation: 「にとって」 = the particle 「に」 (target, standpoint) + 「とって」, the te-form of the verb 「取る」. Literally “taking it into A's hands to look at” → “weighing it from A's position” → “for A”. Because it weighs what something means or is worth to A, it's followed by evaluative predicates (「大切だ」, 「難しい」, 「ありがたい」, 「必要だ」), not by actions done to A. 「は」 adds contrast (「私にとっては」 = for me, at least), and 「の」 lets it modify a noun (「私にとっての幸せ」).

similar.title: 〜にしたら・〜にすれば
similar.explanation: 「にしたら／にすれば」 means “putting yourself in someone's shoes”, often to guess at others' feelings: 「親にしたら心配だろう」; 「にとって」 is a general “for ...” evaluation.

similar.title: 〜として
similar.explanation: 「として」 marks a role or capacity: 「教師として働く」; 「にとって」 marks the standpoint of an evaluation: 「教師にとって大切なこと」.

similar.title: 〜に対して
similar.explanation: 「に対して」 is followed by an attitude or action toward someone: 「子どもに対して厳しい」; 「にとって」 is followed by an evaluation: 「子どもにとって難しい」.

similar.title: 〜から見ると・〜からすると
similar.explanation: 「から見ると」 means “judging from the viewpoint of”, focusing on perspective or opinion: 「外国人から見ると不思議だ」; 「にとって」 focuses on what something means or is worth to someone.
